proof_attempt_summary: Discovery generalized the two-cohort problem to uniformly bounded normalized public weight arrays and fixed common bounded outcomes, with matching cubic-moment sharp upper and unrestricted lower calculations. The final mathematical referee passed with no findings and all six cited sources verified-attested, but the projected paper-score ceiling 7.2 fell below the fixed field gate 7.4 and an independent validity audit confirmed banking at subfield. Two rubric-ballast findings remain preserved; formalization never started, so this bank contains no Lean proof or kernel/axiom certification.
tldr: For any deterministic nonnegative public weights normalized to sum to the fixed cohort size and bounded by a common finite \(W\), the sharp binary treatment-randomization minimax MSE is \(\mu_{2,N}/N-C_A\mu_{3,N}^{2/3}N^{-4/3}+o_W(N^{-4/3})\), uniformly over the full bounded-weight class. Independent fair assignment and a finite-computable square-weight Airy correction attain it; an original-record converse covers all outcome-independent joint designs and arbitrary biased randomized estimators. The original two-cohort coefficient is \(C_A(1+3\kappa^2)^{2/3}\), uniformly for \(\kappa\in[0,1]\). A common finite outcome interval transfers exactly by its squared length.
